judge: Two judges, each a Claude agent shown only the match sheet's claims and truth, not which method made the claims, ruled on every claim without seeing each other's rulings. An adjudicating agent ruled on each claim where they differed. Rules: the same problem at the same place; a general claim states nothing; when unsure, no match.

matches.note: Names only the first floor (G1.1) and the building in general ('exceeds single-exit allowances in stories'). It names no fourth or fifth floor, so the check 11 items are not stated (Rules 2 and 4). It says a stair is shown on G1.1, which is the opposite of stair_discharge.

Same Stair 1 marker on G1.3, same 63-person value, flagged as an undersized stair. The claim compares it to the 44-inch minimum and the 46-inch width on other sheets, not to the 90-person load. That is different wording for the same undersized marker.
The G0.1 index lists A7.1 and the set has no such sheet. This is the same defect at the same index entry.
Door 1001 size versus the exit width calculations. No truth item covers Door 1001.
Fire ratings missing for doors and the stair enclosure. No truth item covers this.
Stair 1 is not shown on the first floor plan A1.1, the level of exit discharge. This is the same defect at the same floor.

Same door 4014, scheduled as a pocket door, flagged as wrong, with a swinging door required. The truth says the plan draws a swing arc. The claim gets there through code and does not cite the plan's swing arc, but the defect is the same: the wrong scheduled type for 4014.
Window sill height and fall protection. No truth item covers this.
General Chapter 10 items (travel distance, dead ends, signage) not shown on G1.2. There is no specific discrepancy, and no fourth or fifth floor stair count is named.
